clue.text: It's back to the fifties for all that

indicators.note: back tells us to read the letters of It's from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give LL

explanation.surface: Someone insists that, despite everything, it's a return to the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses It's; the plural 'fifties' gives two Roman L's, not a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean nevertheless or even so, used to concede a point before qualifying it.

clue.text: Moving anything but smartly limbs hang loosely

indicators.note: hanging loosely suggests the letters of the two words are slackened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shuffling figure moves clumsily, arms and legs dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges LIMBSHANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in an awkward, shuffling, ungainly way is the opposite of moving smartly.

clue.text: Thought the trainee quite perfect

parts.note: a thought is an idea
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone thought the new recruit was flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a model of excellence, beyond improvement, is perfect.

clue.text: She'll wait on no man!

parts.note: reads like a proud feminist boast, but describes a female servant who attends only her mistress

explanation.surface: A defiant woman declares she will not serve any man.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal maid attends a woman, helping her dress, so she never waits on a man.

clue.text: He's regarded as a villain for cutting the discount

indicators.note: cutting means the word for 'for' slices into the discount word

parts.note: a rebate is a discount or partial refund
pro means in favour of, i.e. for

explanation.surface: Someone who slashes a discount is seen as a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' splits the discount word after its first two letters to take in PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or unprincipled scoundrel is generally seen as a villain.

clue.text: Soldiers weary, so get withdrawn

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
weary means tired

explanation.surface: Exhausted troops decide to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retiring is reserved and shy, so the past form describes a withdrawn person.

clue.text: Housed in a camp as chalets are built for Easter

indicators.note: housed in says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Holiday chalets put up in a camp ready for the Easter break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housed in' points to the letters spanning camP AS CHALets.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the Passover or to the festival of the Resurrection, so it means of or for Easter.

clue.text: Turned over a boy's comic — no end of a series

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing, so no

indicators.note: turned over tells us to read the letters of a and the comic's name backwards

parts.note: The Gem was a British weekly story paper for boys, home of Tom Merry

explanation.surface: A child flicks through his comic, the last issue in a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reverses A GEM to MEGA, placed after O. The Gem was a British boys' weekly paper (1907-1939).
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the final item in any sequence.

clue.text: Nowadays charge for entrance

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, so nowadays
a charge or assigned task is a mission

explanation.surface: These days there's a fee to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an entry fee, which is in the surface, but it supplies the task word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed in, or the right of entry, is entrance.

clue.text: Sign on register

definitions.meaning: to put one's name down to join a course or group
to formally record oneself as a member

explanation.definitionFit: Joining a class or roll by putting down one's name is both signing on and registering.

clue.text: Don't cease making up such stories

indicators.note: making up suggests the letters are composed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Keep inventing tales without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making up' rearranges DONTCEASE; 'such' ties the definition to the made-up tales of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Short amusing accounts of real incidents are told as stories.

clue.text: An American takes wood with some hesitation

parts.note: elm is a type of wood
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A US citizen hesitantly picks up some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmer is a typically American first name, so it stands for an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name especially associated with the United States, as in Elmer Fudd, can stand for a typical American.

clue.text: A precious stone — not first grade, unfortunately

parts.note: the first grade is A, so the next grade down is B
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Sadly, a gem turns out to be of inferior quality.
explanation.walkthrough: A balas is a delicate rose-red variety of spinel ruby.
explanation.definitionFit: This rose-coloured spinel is a gemstone, sometimes called a ruby.

clue.text: What a judge does in actual practice

indicators.note: in places the judge's activity within the word for actual

parts.note: actual means real
a judge hears cases

explanation.surface: A remark about how judges behave in the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in actual practice' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container indicator, and 'practice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through before a performance is a practice session.

clue.text: Rage against sovereign and country

parts.note: ire means anger, rage
a sovereign was a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for a pound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Anger directed at the monarch and the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, hence L (libra).
explanation.definitionFit: The island state of Eire is a nation.

clue.text: Laboured to be a real reformer

indicators.note: a reformer remakes things, so these letters are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone toiled hard to become a genuine reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformer' rearranges TOBEAREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overworked, highly detailed or contrived describes something laboured.

clue.text: Pests surround a person refusing drink that's light

indicators.note: surround means the pests word encloses the other letters

parts.note: lice are pests
TT means teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Insects swarm round a teetotaller who is a lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surround' is the container indicator. 'light' is a window, and a lattice window has criss-cross panes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross window, and a window is a light in architectural usage.

clue.text: Time to get up put off

parts.note: tempo is the time or speed of a piece of music
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: An alarm call that is then postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall or delay deciding, in order to gain time, is to put things off.

clue.text: Worked out cut Her Majesty's accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the cut word takes in the royal letters

parts.note: excised means cut out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone worked out that the Queen had approved the cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her Majesty's accepted' reads as 'Her Majesty has accepted': 'accepted' puts ER into EXCISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising the body, or a matter, is working it out, by training or by thinking hard.

clue.text: Give pleasure to tot in depression

indicators.note: in places the tot word inside the valley word

parts.note: a glen is a valley, a depression in the land
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Cheer up a small child who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child and 'depression' low spirits; they are 'add up' and a valley, with 'in' as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone happy or cheerful is to give them pleasure.

clue.text: Few follow Number One, which is disgusting

indicators.note: follow places the word for few after the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
some means a few

explanation.surface: A handful trail behind the leader, which is revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul-smelling and offensive is disgusting.

clue.text: A novel more can read in translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading a foreign book in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges MORECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A long prose story of adventure or love is a novel.

clue.text: Set and let hair curl

parts.note: a ring is a set or clique of people
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the hairdresser's, a set lets the hair curl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' hints at a hairdo, but it is RING, a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spiral lock of hair is a curl.

clue.text: Support for formal proposal

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
a motion is a formal proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Backing for a motion put before a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting something, publicising and championing it, is supporting it.

clue.text: Go wholeheartedly for roly-poly

definitions.meaning: to opt firmly and decisively for one choice

explanation.surface: Someone throws themselves enthusiastically into a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Roly-poly is also a British jam pudding, which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for is to opt firmly for, and a roly-poly figure is chubby.

clue.text: A decoration half resembling daggers

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word for resembling is kept

parts.note: like means resembling

explanation.surface: A medal shaped somewhat like daggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps LI of LIKE. Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in printing.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's dagger symbol is an obelus, and plural daggers are these marks.

clue.text: Work on muscular disorder of the eye

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a tic is an involuntary muscle spasm

explanation.surface: Treating a twitch around the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to vision or the visual organ.

clue.text: French city network

definitions.meaning: a town in the Correze department of central France
a fine mesh fabric of silk or nylon

explanation.definitionFit: The town gave its name to the fine netted fabric used for veils and ballet skirts.

clue.text: The employment of superior natural flavouring

parts.note: U means upper class, superior
sage is a herb used for flavour

explanation.surface: Putting a fine herb to work in cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is used, its use, is its employment.

clue.text: Not where olives are grown!

parts.note: olives yield oil, so groves might be called ..., but the term means land producing petroleum

explanation.surface: A remark that some fields of oil have nothing to do with olives.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas producing crude petroleum share their name with what olive groves might jokingly be called.

clue.text: A top man's pride sent crashing

indicators.note: crashing suggests the letters smash and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A leader's arrogance brought down in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges PRIDESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a republic or organisation is its top man.

clue.text: Correct a leading journalist taking people in

indicators.note: taking with 'in' means the journalist abbreviation holds the people word

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief journalist
men are people

explanation.surface: An editor fixes copy by bringing staff in.
explanation.walkthrough: The container indicator is split: 'taking' and the closing 'in' together say the people go inside the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct it by revising errors.
